svg.text: K4b P1: PRESS + VERTICAL LATHE — the column pushes, T turns, the arm places tools
The press holds no tools: the arm sets a piston, corer or tailstock cup on the work, and the plate pushes it.
press: pull-down column, 2.5 kN, stroke 250, 90° swing by a helical cam
T: Ø 70 thimble, 15 Nm, 0–600 rpm · S: Ø 36, 0–12 000 rpm (both canned)
P1: 3 kW induction ring round a Ø 75 hole · 3 load cells ±2 g
peel/core/stone with 3 mechanisms: lathe, press family, knurled disc
A SIDE SECTION through P1 and the press (rear wall left, door right)

text.tspan: DICE: the arm sets the comb piston; the press pushes 1–2 kN through the 6 mm grid
RICE: potatoes boiled in skin, ricer plate, 1–1.5 kN: the skins stay in the tube
LATHE: the press holds the tailstock cup, T turns, the arm’s peeler traverses down

svg.text: Also: tube corers, corer-wedger, pitter, garlic and Spätzle plates, press-peel ring.

T turns pots, bowls and plates: stirs and kneads under hung scrapers, spins salad,
spin-coats pancakes, lathe for peeling, polar plating. S drives the blender jug rotor.

g.text: 1/3 Dice: E halves the onion at the blade, the halves drop into the tube; the press pushes them through the grid into the bowl
2/3 Rice: potatoes boiled in their skins go into the tube with the ricer plate; the flesh comes out, the skins stay
3/3 Lathe: the press holds the fruit on the turning spike cup; the arm’s sprung peeler follows the surface down; peel falls into the dish
